title: Which clock the Japanese regiment's report keeps

basis: Japanese army records are usually read as Tokyo time. The report's sunrise falls within two minutes of the sun's at UTC+8 and an hour from Tokyo time's, and its 18:40 dusk only fits local time; the times the two sides both record (the east gate at about 14:00, the west gate at 17:00) agree on it.

title: Whether the guns duelled on 27 March
reading: Chinese field-gun fire on Liujiahu at 17:30 and 19:15; no duel
basis: The Japanese report on 27 March records Chinese shells on Liujiahu but no counter-battery fire, which is first ordered for the 28th; the Chinese account gives no hour.

title: Where the Chinese 15 cm howitzers stood
reading: South of Xiongshan, about 13 km from the Japanese guns at Sanlizhuang, within 5 km
basis: In the direction the Japanese saw the rounds come from, and beyond the reach of every Japanese gun from its position, as Ohashi remembered; within the 15 km that reaches Liujiahu and Sanlizhuang, where the rounds fell.

title: When the Chinese 15 cm howitzers first fired
reading: Their first fire the Japanese recorded: 15:46 on 31 March
basis: The Chinese account's duel of the 27th has no counterpart in the 63rd Infantry's or the Type 96 company's reports, which describe the guns of the 28th as field guns. Both sides' times are on local time, so the days cannot be a clock's error.
